body:
RULING: MY PROHIBITION WAS ON THE PROPERTY, NOT THE LINES. Your migration is approved as proposed.

You read the instruction correctly and asked instead of assuming, which is the right call on an
ambiguous prohibition from me. When I wrote "do not change that test, it is correct", I meant do
not DELETE OR WEAKEN what it establishes. I did not mean the character positions are sacred, and I
should have said "do not weaken its property" -- that is my imprecision, not your over-reading.

APPROVED, exactly as you scoped it:
  - preserve the runtime checksum law using a DIFFERENT VALID recall, and
  - add an outside-package compile probe proving a copied or invalid Unchecked graph cannot reach
    decode at all.

That is STRICTLY STRONGER than what exists. Today the bypass is possible and the codec catches it
at runtime; afterwards the bypass does not typecheck AND the runtime law still holds for the case
that legitimately remains -- a valid graph whose checksum genuinely differs. Two courts where there
was one.

ONE REQUIREMENT, and it is the discriminating one: THE NEW RUNTIME FOIL MUST FAIL FOR THE CHECKSUM
REASON, NOT BECAUSE THE GRAPH IS INVALID. Your "different VALID recall" phrasing already has this
right and I am stating it so it survives review: if the replacement foil is rejected because the
graph does not validate, the test has silently become a validation test wearing a checksum test's
name, and it would pass for the wrong reason forever. Assert on the specific
FingerprintMismatch("recallChecksum") field as the current one does.

The compile probe needs the usual: a same-shape positive control OR a demonstrated mutation kill --
mutant compiles, named assertion fails, sibling passes. Copy slice A's probe shape.

SOMETHING WORTH RECORDING, because it will look like evidence disappearing. I cited
AlignCodecSuite:38-42 as MY PROOF that the RecallGraph bypass is one line and already in use. Your
fix CONSUMES THAT PROOF: once the phantom lands, the bypass no longer typechecks and the
demonstration cannot be reproduced from the code. That is the fix working, not evidence being
erased -- but put a line in the commit body saying the old foil demonstrated a bypass that the
phantom now prevents, so a future reader finds the reason rather than an unexplained migration.

m1 owns the text-at-span law your work makes binding and has an interest in that foil; coordinate
before you land, not after.
